description: During Phase 4A (guardrail wiring), a Rigby sub-agent ran a read-only `git status` while listing new files, despite the explicit constraint to run no git commands and the git skill's standing rule that `git status` is forbidden (it writes .git/index.lock as part of its index refresh; on FUSE mounts that lock orphans and blocks all git operations). No other git command was run; no lock file remained after the session (verified: no .git/index.lock or .git/HEAD.lock present).
correction: Never run `git status` in any agent context; use the lock-free alternatives (`git diff --name-only HEAD`, `git ls-files --modified --others --exclude-standard`) or plain filesystem listing (`ls`, `find`). Sub-agent briefs must state the lock-free alternatives, not just the prohibition, so the fallback is not improvised.
systemic_fix: Add the lock-free alternatives to the standing sub-agent constraint template used in Phase dispatch prompts (prohibition + named alternative commands), so the next dispatch does not rely on the sub-agent remembering the skill text.
